description: Three independent guards. (1) Commit guard (commit-guard.sh, PreToolUse). Claude Code permissions.ask rules, installed by setup, prompt the human for every foreground git commit, git push, and pull request merge. The guard refuses a sub-agent's commit or push, a merge by a sub-agent or by the pipeline, a push that forces or deletes, and any of them behind bash -c, sh -c, env, eval, a leading NAME=value, or a program path, which the ask rules cannot see. It catches mistakes and is not a security boundary. (2) Pipeline scope (pipeline-scope.sh, PermissionRequest). For the scheduled pipeline only, marked by WORKBENCH_DEV_TEAM_PIPELINE=1 on the process bin/dispatch-agent.sh spawns, it allows a prompt for one plain git -C <dir>, rm, or rmdir command when every path is absolute and stays inside the roots: all of $TMPDIR, where every mktemp -d folder lands, so another run's clone is in scope too, and the scratch roots. The git subcommand must be add, checkout, commit, diff, log, merge, or push. It never allows a pull request merge, a force push, a push to the default branch, or a command a user deny rule matches. (3) Local-review guard — while a Holmes Local-mode review is in flight, that session's sub-agents may read the human's working tree and run its test suite, and may not write into it, through Bash or through Edit, Write, or NotebookEdit. Each guard owns its own matcher blocks; none reads another's state.
